label: Task-22
title: Add backend API to get nodes with most edges (hub nodes)
description:
Create a new backend API endpoint that returns nodes sorted by their edge count (connectivity).

## Use Case
In the graph viewer, users need a way to quickly find the most connected nodes (hubs) to use as starting points for exploration. Currently, the graph viewer shows an empty state with no suggestions.

## Proposed API

```
GET /nodes/api/nodes/hubs?limit=10&min_edges=2
```

## Response Format
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "hubs": [
    { "label": "Feature-12", "title": "Graph Visualization", "node_type": "feature", "edge_count": 15 },
    { "label": "Version-1", "title": "v0.1.4", "node_type": "version", "edge_count": 12 },
    { "label": "Task-15", "title": "D3.js component", "node_type": "task", "edge_count": 8 }
  ]
}
```

## UI Integration
1. Call this API when graph viewer loads without a root node
2. Display hub nodes as clickable suggestions:
   ```
   No graph loaded. Try these connected nodes:
   - Feature-12 (15 connections)
   - Version-1 (12 connections)
   - Task-15 (8 connections)
   ```
3. Clicking a hub loads that node's graph

## Backend Implementation Notes
- Iterate all nodes and count links array length
- Sort by count descending
- Return top N with min_edges filter
